title.narrative: Proportion of confirmed malaria cases that received first-line antimalarial treatment in private sector health facilities

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the proportion of confirmed malaria cases attending private sector health facilities who receive the recommended first-line antimalarial treatment in accordance with national treatment guidelines. It reflects the quality of malaria case management within the private sector, including adherence to treatment protocols and availability of appropriate medicines.
Numerator: Number of confirmed malaria cases in private sector health facilities who received first-line antimalarial treatment according to national guidelines Denominator: Total number of confirmed malaria cases in private sector health facilities
Calculation Formula: (Proportion of confirmed cases treated) = (Numerator / Denominator) × 100
Unit of Measurement: Percentage (%)
Data Collection Method: Routine data collection from private health facilities, compiled through reporting mechanisms where available and integrated into the national malaria information system
Interpretation: Higher values indicate strong adherence to national malaria treatment guidelines within the private sector and effective integration of private providers in malaria case management. Lower values may suggest drug stock-outs, gaps in provider compliance, weak reporting systems, or limited regulatory oversight.

title.narrative: Proportion of suspected malaria cases tested with a parasitological test in private sector health facilities

description.narrative: This indicator measures the proportion of suspected malaria cases attending private sector health facilities who receive a parasitological test (microscopy or rapid diagnostic test – RDT) to confirm malaria diagnosis. It reflects access to and utilization of malaria diagnostic services in the private sector, as well as adherence to national malaria testing guidelines.

title.narrative: Proportion of suspected malaria cases tested with a parasitological test in public sector health facilities

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the proportion of suspected malaria cases attending public sector health facilities who receive a parasitological test (either microscopy or rapid diagnostic test – RDT) to confirm malaria diagnosis. It reflects adherence to national malaria diagnostic guidelines and the availability and utilization of testing services within public health facilities. A high proportion indicates strong compliance with the “test before treat” policy and improved quality of malaria case management.
Numerator: Number of suspected malaria cases in public sector health facilities who received a parasitological test (microscopy or RDT) Denominator: Total number of suspected malaria cases attending public sector health facilities
Calculation Formula: (Proportion of suspected cases tested) = (Numerator / Denominator) × 100
Unit of Measurement: Percentage (%)
Data Source: National malaria database (PNCM)
Interpretation: Higher values indicate better compliance with malaria testing guidelines and improved diagnostic coverage. Values below target may suggest stock-outs of RDTs, gaps in training, or poor adherence to protocols.

title.narrative: Proportion of suspected malaria cases tested with a parasitological test in the community

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the proportion of suspected malaria cases identified at the community level (e.g., by community health workers) who receive a parasitological test (rapid diagnostic test – RDT) to confirm malaria diagnosis. It reflects access to diagnostic services at community level and adherence to national malaria guidelines. A high value indicates strong coverage of community-based testing and compliance with the “test before treat” policy.
Numerator: Number of suspected malaria cases in the community who received a parasitological test (RDT) Denominator: Total number of suspected malaria cases identified in the community
Calculation Formula: (Proportion of suspected cases tested) = (Numerator / Denominator) × 100
Unit of Measurement: Percentage (%)
Data Collection Method: Routine data collection by community health workers, compiled through reporting tools and integrated into the national malaria information system
Interpretation: Higher values indicate strong access to malaria diagnostic services at community level and good adherence to testing protocols. Lower values may suggest RDT stock-outs, limited CHW coverage, or gaps in training and supervision.

title.narrative: Number of insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) distributed continuously to targeted at-risk groups

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the number of insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) distributed through routine/continuous distribution channels to targeted at-risk populations, such as pregnant women and children under five. It reflects the performance of routine vector control interventions aimed at maintaining adequate coverage and protecting vulnerable groups.
Numerator: Total number of insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) distributed to targeted at-risk groups through continuous distribution channels
Unit of Measurement: Number
Data Collection Method: Routine data collection from health facilities and distribution points, compiled through the national health information system
Interpretation: Higher values indicate strong implementation of routine ITN distribution systems and improved protection of vulnerable populations. Lower values may suggest supply chain issues, stock-outs, low service utilization, or gaps in service delivery.

title.narrative: Percentage of malaria foci that received a complete investigation and were recorded in accordance with national guidelines

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the percentage of identified malaria transmission foci (hotspots) that have undergone a complete focus investigation and have been properly recorded in accordance with national surveillance guidelines. It reflects the performance of malaria surveillance and response systems in detecting, investigating, and documenting transmission foci.
Numerator: Number of identified malaria foci that received a complete investigation and were recorded according to national guidelines Denominator: Total number of identified malaria foci
Calculation Formula: (Percentage of foci investigated and recorded) = (Numerator / Denominator) × 100
Unit of Measurement: Percentage (%)
Data Collection Method: Routine surveillance data collection through focus investigation tools, compiled and validated at departmental and national levels
Higher values indicate strong surveillance and response systems, with effective identification and investigation of malaria transmission foci—critical for malaria elimination. Lower values may suggest gaps in field investigation capacity, delays in response, or weaknesses in data recording and reporting systems

title.narrative: Percentage of confirmed malaria cases that received a complete investigation and were recorded in accordance with national guidelines

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the percentage of confirmed malaria cases in strata 1, 2, and 3 that have undergone a complete case investigation and have been recorded in accordance with national surveillance guidelines. It assesses the effectiveness of surveillance systems in ensuring systematic case investigation and accurate reporting across transmission settings.
Numerator: Number of confirmed malaria cases that received a complete investigation and were recorded according to national guidelines (Strata 1, 2 and 3) Denominator: Total number of confirmed malaria cases (Strata 1, 2 and 3)
Calculation Formula: (Percentage of cases investigated and recorded) = (Numerator / Denominator) × 100
Unit of Measurement: Percentage (%)
Data Collection Method: Routine surveillance data collection through case investigation tools, compiled and validated at district/departmental and national levels
Interpretation: Higher values indicate strong malaria surveillance and case investigation systems, essential for malaria elimination. Lower values may suggest gaps in follow-up, limited surveillance capacity, delays in investigation, or weaknesses in data recording and reporting systems.

title.narrative: Proportion of confirmed malaria cases that received first-line antimalarial treatment in public sector health facilities

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the proportion of confirmed malaria cases in public sector health facilities who receive the recommended first-line antimalarial treatment in accordance with national treatment guidelines. It reflects the quality of malaria case management, including adherence to treatment protocols and availability of appropriate antimalarial medicines.
Numerator: Number of confirmed malaria cases in public sector health facilities who received first-line antimalarial treatment according to national guidelines Denominator: Total number of confirmed malaria cases in public sector health facilities
Calculation Formula: (Proportion of confirmed cases treated) = (Numerator / Denominator) × 100
Unit of Measurement: Percentage (%)
Interpretation: Higher values indicate strong adherence to national malaria treatment guidelines and effective case management. Lower values may suggest stock-outs of antimalarial drugs, gaps in clinical practice, or data quality/reporting issues.

title.narrative: Proportion of confirmed malaria cases that received first-line antimalarial treatment in the community

description.narrative:
This indicator measures the proportion of confirmed malaria cases at the community level (e.g., managed by community health workers) who receive the recommended first-line antimalarial treatment in accordance with national guidelines. It reflects the effectiveness of community-based case management, including timely treatment and adherence to treatment protocols.
Numerator: Number of confirmed malaria cases in the community who received first-line antimalarial treatment according to national guidelines Denominator: Total number of confirmed malaria cases in the community
Calculation Formula: (Proportion of confirmed cases treated) = (Numerator / Denominator) × 100
Unit of Measurement: Percentage (%)
Data Collection Method: Routine data collection by community health workers, compiled through reporting tools and integrated into the national malaria information system
Interpretation: Higher values indicate effective community-based malaria case management and adherence to treatment guidelines. Lower values may suggest stock-outs of antimalarial drugs, delays in treatment, gaps in CHW training, or weaknesses in supervision and reporting.
